task.description: WF-03 step 6b, TEST-DESIGNER, REWORK of your step 06 by the list of remarks of the gate (handoffs/ISS-0092-20261117-01/step-07-test-design-validator.json, verdict FAIL at pass 1 of 3). Only these four remarks, nothing else (AP-019). F1 (Medium, required): SV-68 (pixel-office-server.test.js, helper `rawHeadStatus`) and NF-07 (node-floor.test.js, helper `rawHead`) never check that the server closes the connection after the 431; the helpers resolve after a 10 s destroy timer and return only the status, so the validator's mutants D05 (Pixel Office server) and D06 (team web server), a clientError handler that leaves the socket open, stay green. Fix: make both helpers return `closedByServer` (true when the connection ended before the destroy timer fired) and assert it for the 2 500-line probe in both tests (criterion 7: «closes the connection»), keeping the existing status assertions; the 10 s timer stays only as the safety net and must not make the test slow when the server behaves (it resolves as soon as the socket closes). F3 (Low, do it): NF-05c takes the expected exit code from the imported NODE_REFUSAL_EXIT, so the mutant NODE_REFUSAL_EXIT = 3 (R07) is caught only by NF-04's pin: write the literal 2 (the value the design fixes) in the NF-05 rows that compare the exit code. F2 (Low, do it if it stays small): a guard moved behind a pure parse of the arguments survives in the programs without a help (A-E5 web/main.js, W-E1 cli.js, W-E11 office-report.js) because every row uses valid calls: add three twin rows under the old Node (22.21.1 as the other rows use) with a WRONG call each, which must still be answered by the refusal line of the guard (design section 3 says the guard stands before the dispatch of every command): if the design or README line 9 says the opposite for these three (a wrong call is answered as on any Node), do NOT add the rows and instead name this as a limit in result.issues with the line you read. F4 (Low): NF-05a hard-codes the counts 14 and 23 by design: add one comment line at the constant saying that adding a script means updating it, and nothing else. After the edit prove with your own scripts (outside the project, as in step 06) that D05 and D06 and R07 are now red and that no earlier mutant went green, and that the unmutated tests are green on the current code; run `npx prettier --check` and `npx eslint --max-warnings 0` on the changed files in a fresh clone (they do not run the tests); print the counts of test( registrations and assert. occurrences before and after (not lower). Do NOT run the tests, npm run check or node --test (decisions/0110). Fill result with the changes per remark, the mutant results, the counts, must_be_proved_on_github, the issues. Be economical. RULES OF THIS PC (decisions/0110, 0127, 0129): do NOT run npm run check, cd app && npm run ..., node --test, the tools test scripts or the e2e tests; the record of a test run is read from GitHub with gh run view (read-only). Allowed: cd tools && npm run -s traces and handoffs-check; read-only git and gh; your own scripts and fresh clones (git clone -c core.autocrlf=false, npm ci) only in your own folder under <scratch> (the real path is in the message that launched you). Node 22 first on PATH (<node22>). A server you start binds port 0 or a free high port and is stopped by its exact process id; never bind, probe or stop the ports 4780, 4781, 4782 and 4790. One browser at a time on this PC. No git commit, push, pull, checkout, stash, reset or tag. LF line endings. Never write the name of the reference product, nor a path of this computer, into a Sai file or a handoff (write <scratch> or <outside the project>). Fill only the result of your handoff; the top-level status stays PENDING and completed_at null: ORCH closes. English.

remarks.change: Both helpers (rawHead in node-floor.test.js, rawHeadStatus in pixel-office-server.test.js) now set a flag in the 10 s safety-net timer before it destroys the socket and return closedByServer: !timedOut; the promise still resolves on the socket's close event, so a server that behaves costs no time (NF-07 340 ms, SV-68 40 ms in the harness, as before). NF-07 (for team web and the picker) and SV-68 assert closedByServer === true for the 2 500-line probe, after the existing 431 assertion; all earlier status assertions are kept.
remarks.proof: D05 (Pixel Office: a clientError handler writes the 431 and leaves the socket open) -> red in SV-68 with the message 'the connection stays open after the 431 | false !== true'; D06 (the same on the team web server) -> red in NF-07 with 'team web: the connection stays open after the 431'. Both were green before the rework (validator's finding).

remarks.change: NF-05c now compares the exit code with the literal 2 (row.code ?? 2; the Pixel Office rows keep their literal 1). The import NODE_REFUSAL_EXIT stays for NF-04's pin.
remarks.proof: R07 (NODE_REFUSAL_EXIT = 3) -> red in NF-04 and now also in NF-05c ('prepare-run under 22.21.1: code 3').

remarks.reason: The instruction says to add the three wrong-call rows unless the design or README line 9 says the opposite. README line 9 (tools/README.md, the line that starts 'The one check command (quality-bar Q4)') says: 'on another Node a node <file> script ... that is started to do its work stops at once, ... while `--help` and a wrong call are answered as on any Node'; the design says the same in section 8 (line 9 text) and in its failure table ('A wrong call on such a Node, for the five commands whose parsing comes before the help: the usage line, code 2'), while its section 3 puts the guard before parseArgs for cli.js, web/main.js and office-report.js. So the two documents disagree for these three programs, and the README states the wrong call is answered as on any Node: a row that expects the refusal line for a wrong call would contradict it, and a row that expects the usage line would pin the guard behind the parse, which is what the gate wants to forbid. The decision is not mine; it is the reviewer's open question I3 of step 05b (a dated addendum to decisions/0120 О5 and the README wording).
